Title: Card Number Iframe Isolation
Preconditions:
[PRE:CLEAR_SESSION]
[PRE:SIGNIN_AS:USER_DEFAULT]
- CyberSource payment form displayed
- Browser DevTools open
Steps:
[NAV] {{FRONT_URL}}/cart - confirm the CyberSource card-payment form is displayed
[WAIT] the Card Number field finishes loading (CyberSource Flex Microform mounts into #cardNumber-container)
[KEY] inspect #cardNumber-container and record whether its rendered child is an <iframe> (per vc-frontend client-app/shared/payment/components/payment-processing-cyber-source.vue number.load(...)) or a plain <input> owned by the storefront page
[ACT] click into the Card Number iframe field and type @td(CYBERSOURCE_VISA.number)
[KEY] capture the storefront page own DOM/JS state after typing, excluding the iframe internal cross-origin document
Assertions:
[DOM] #cardNumber-container only rendered child is an <iframe> element - the field is not a same-origin <input> in the storefront page own DOM
[STATE] the typed card number does not appear anywhere in the storefront page own DOM outside the iframe (no attribute, hidden input or text node carries the digits)
[CONSOLE] no cross-origin/SecurityError is thrown when the SDK initializes or the page interacts with the container
Cross_Layer_Checks: [NETWORK] no request fired by the storefront page own JS (outside the iframe) carries the typed card number
Failure_Signals: Card Number field renders as a plain <input> in the storefront page own DOM (no iframe); the typed card number is readable from the parent page DOM or JS scope; console throws a cross-origin/SecurityError on field init
Cleanup: none - no order created
References: PCI-DSS SAQ A client-side field isolation. Grounded in vc-frontend client-app/shared/payment/components/payment-processing-cyber-source.vue (#cardNumber-container, number.load(...), CyberSource Flex Microform), source fetched live 2026-09-19. Business_Rule cleared: BL-SEC-00N does not exist (no BL-SEC-* family in the oracle) and no promoted invariant covers this behaviour - oracle gap, candidate for /qa-review-oracles.

Title: CVV Field Is A Processor-Hosted Iframe And Card Data Reaches The Platform Only As An Opaque Token
Preconditions:
[PRE:SIGNIN_AS:USER_DEFAULT]
- CyberSource form ready: a line item is in the cart and the 'Bank card (CyberSource)' payment method is selected
Steps:
[NAV] {{FRONT_URL}}/cart - confirm the CyberSource card-payment form is displayed
[WAIT] the CVV field (#securityCode-container) finishes loading
[KEY] inspect #securityCode-container and record its rendered child and the child's title attribute
[ACT] fill the Card Number iframe field with @td(CYBERSOURCE_VISA.number), Cardholder Name with @td(CYBERSOURCE_VISA.cardholder), the expiry fields with @td(CYBERSOURCE_VISA.expiry) and the CVV iframe field with @td(CYBERSOURCE_VISA.cvv)
[ACT] submit payment
[WAIT] the authorizePayment GraphQL response is received
[CAPTURE] the createToken request to CyberSource and the authorizePayment mutation request to {{BACK_URL}}
Assertions:
[DOM] #securityCode-container holds an iframe with title 'secure payment field' - the CVV is rendered by the processor-hosted Flex Microform, not by a storefront <input> {OBSERVED} (KB-4B419313)
[BODY] the authorizePayment mutation parameters array is a single {key: token, value: <JWT>} entry - no cardNumber, cvv or securityCode parameter, and the typed CVV digits appear in no request body sent to {{BACK_URL}} {OBSERVED} (KB-4B419313)
[STATUS] authorizePayment returns its documented success shape with no 4xx/5xx
Cross_Layer_Checks:
[CONSOLE] no TypeError or JS errors from the microform field
[API] the token JWT carries only a masked PAN (last 4), bin and expiry, with an empty securityCode {OBSERVED}
Failure_Signals: #securityCode-container holds a plain storefront <input> instead of the processor-hosted iframe; the authorizePayment parameters carry a raw card number, CVV or securityCode field instead of only an opaque token; the typed CVV digits appear in any request body sent to the platform; the token JWT carries a non-empty securityCode
Cleanup: Cancel/void the order via admin if one was created
References: Re-aligned 2026-10-28 (REG-2026-10-28-1013 triage): the former masking assertion is retired - the CyberSource-hosted Flex Microform iframe renders the CVV digits unmasked and that is accepted (KB-1F264839); the case now asserts what the storefront controls: the hosted iframe and a token-only authorizePayment (KB-4B419313). Title: Session Token Security - Signed, Short-Lived, No Secrets In Claims
Preconditions:
[PRE:SIGNIN_AS:USER_DEFAULT]
- The storefront token is requested through the endpoint the sign-in form uses (POST /connect/token, KB-0407F36E)
Steps:
[AUTH] role=USER_DEFAULT: POST {{FRONT_URL}}/connect/token (password grant, scope offline_access, storeId={{STORE_ID}}) and keep access_token, refresh_token, expires_in
[KEY] decode (do not verify) the access_token header and payload
[GQL] query { me { userName } } on {{FRONT_URL}}/graphql with the valid access_token (baseline)
[GQL] the same query with (a) the payload segment edited (role and sub changed, signature kept), (b) alg=none and an empty signature, (c) the exp claim edited into the past with the signature kept, (d) the literal Bearer abc.def.ghi
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/users with the valid storefront token, then with (a)
Cross_Layer_Checks:
[NETWORK] on the storefront the token travels in the Authorization header of /graphql requests, never in a query string {OBSERVED}
[CONSOLE] no token or password is logged
Failure_Signals: Edited-payload, alg=none, expired or garbage token still resolves to the original or an elevated identity; a secret claim (password hash, security stamp) in the payload; token lifetime far above 1800 s; refresh token decodable as a JWT; token present in a URL
Cleanup: none - read-only; the minted token expires by itself
References:
Authored 2026-11-05 (stable-16 W6 repair), grounded live on vcptcore_regression (Platform 3.1076.8, theme 2.59.0) with the lane-1 account: token decode, four forged variants, platform-API audience. KB-7DA9B0B7 (storefront-scoped token refused by platform REST with 401) is DISPUTED - not every REST route refuses it - so the case asserts only /api/platform/security/users.
Where the browser keeps the token (storage vs memory) is NOT asserted - no storage inspection on the MCP lane; see SEC-PCI-005 for the storage method.
Catches: signature or expiry validation bypass - mutants: skip signature check, accept alg=none, ignore exp.
Business_Rule left empty: no BL-SEC-* family exists (oracle gap).

Title: Logout Token Revocation - Refresh Token Dies At Logout
Preconditions:
[PRE:SIGNIN_AS:USER_DEFAULT]
User is logged in to the storefront
- The session under test is THIS browser session only: never use a "sign out everywhere" action
- Whether persistent token validation is on is NOT assumed: it is not a registered platform setting (GET /api/platform/settings/... answers 500 "not registered", KB-7564A9BF) so it is inferred from the last step
Steps:
[KEY] from the sign-in POST /connect/token response capture access_token, refresh_token and expires_in
[ACT] Log out from the storefront (account menu popup, BL-AUTH-007)
[WAIT] Wait for logout to complete and redirect to home or /sign-in
[CAPTURE] the token-revocation request fired on logout
[HTTP] POST {{FRONT_URL}}/connect/token with grant_type=refresh_token and the captured (revoked) refresh_token
[GQL] Reuse the captured access token as the Authorization header on query { me { userName } } against {{FRONT_URL}}/graphql and record userName; this reading decides PERSISTENT_VALIDATION_ENABLED (Anonymous = enabled, the original user = disabled)
Cross_Layer_Checks:
[CONSOLE] no TypeError or JS errors
[NETWORK] no unexpected 5xx
Failure_Signals: Refresh grant succeeds after logout (the refresh token survived - real defect, a stolen refresh token would mint new access tokens forever); no revocation request observed on logout; 500 instead of 400 invalid_grant
Cleanup: none
References:
Rewritten 2026-11-05 (stable-16 W6 repair, REG-2026-11-05-0023-W6R FAIL triage): the old assertion 2 expected the revoked ACCESS token to be rejected. The platform validates access tokens statelessly by default - logout and /revoke/token end the refresh token only (KB-7564A9BF, well attested, re-confirmed on vcptcore_regression 2026-11-05: revoke 200, refresh 400 invalid_grant, access token still 200). The security property that holds by default is refresh-token revocation; access-token rejection is asserted only when persistent validation is on.
Row re-split 2026-09-19 (REG-2026-09-19-1035): a stray trailing quote had swallowed Steps/Assertions into Preconditions. The captured token is storefront-issued (iss=...-storefront, role=__customer) so it is asserted against {{FRONT_URL}}/graphql, not the platform BACK_URL.
Catches: logout that leaves the refresh token valid - mutants: revocation call dropped from logout; revoke endpoint a no-op. Do NOT re-add "revoked access token is rejected" as an unconditional assertion (it asserts a setting, not the product).
Business_Rule left empty: no BL-SEC-* family exists (oracle gap).

- The lockout threshold is read from the failed-attempt responses, not assumed

Steps:
[HTTP] POST {{FRONT_URL}}/connect/token (password grant, storeId={{STORE_ID}}) for {{LOCKOUT_TEST_EMAIL}} with the CORRECT password - baseline, expect a token
[HTTP] POST the same grant with a wrong password 5 times in a row, record the response of each
[HTTP] POST the same grant with the CORRECT password (6th attempt)
[KEY] record code and lockoutEnd / lockoutSecondsRemaining of the 6th response
[NAV] {{FRONT_URL}}/sign-in - sign in as {{LOCKOUT_TEST_EMAIL}} with the correct password and record the visible text of the error
[SETUP] unlock the account: POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/users/{id}/unlock with an administrator token
[HTTP] POST the grant with the CORRECT password again

[STATUS] attempts 1-5 with the wrong password answer 400 invalid_grant with code login_failed and a generic description {DOC} KB-0407F36E (observed on vcst_qa and vcptcore_qa 2026-10-29)
[STATUS] the 6th attempt, with the CORRECT password, is still refused: 400 with code user_is_temporary_locked_out and a lockoutEnd about 15 minutes ahead {DOC} KB-8646A9CB, BL-AUTH-003 (threshold 5 is the platform default; read from the stand, not assumed)
[DOM] the sign-in page shows its generic failure text, not a text that confirms the account exists or says it is locked {DOC} KB-8646A9CB
[STATUS] after the unlock the correct password returns 200 and an access_token {DOC} KB-8646A9CB
Cross_Layer_Checks:
[API] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/users/{id}/locked reports locked=true before the unlock and locked=false after {DOC} alias LOCKOUT_TEST_USERS contract (aliases.json changelog 1.5.9)
[NETWORK] no 5xx on any attempt

Cleanup: Unlock the dedicated account (always, also on failure) via POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/users/{id}/unlock

NOT RUN on vcptcore_regression (REG-2026-11-05-0023-W6R authoring): LOCKOUT_TEST_EMAIL is empty on this environment and a lockout attempt on any shared account is forbidden while another wave runs. Expectations come from KB-8646A9CB and KB-0407F36E (observed on other builds, platform 3.1073-3.1090) and BL-AUTH-003, not from this stand - ground on the first run with the dedicated account (vcst has agent-test-lockout-20260729@test-agent.com).

Title: Persistent Access Token — Revoked Token Returns 401 (State Transition: Active → Revoked)
Preconditions:
[PRE:CLEAR_SESSION]
- Admin credentials available
- Two contexts/tokens can be obtained independently
- The actual value of Authorization__EnablePersistentStorageTokenValidation is VERIFIED LIVE in Steps, never assumed
Steps:
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/settings?names=Authorization.EnablePersistentStorageTokenValidation and record PERSISTENT_VALIDATION_ENABLED
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/connect/token credentials to obtain Token A (access_token + refresh_token)
[WAIT] Receive Token A
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/connect/token again with same credentials to obtain Token B
[WAIT] Receive Token B (separate authorization entry)
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/revoke/token with token=<Token A refresh_token>, token_type_hint=refresh_token, Authorization: Bearer <Token A access_token>
[WAIT] Revocation completes (HTTP 200)
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/users with Authorization: Bearer <Token A access_token>
[WAIT] Receive response
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/users with Authorization: Bearer <Token B access_token>
[WAIT] Receive response (expect 200)
Assertions:
[STATUS] POST /revoke/token returns HTTP 200
[STATUS] IF PERSISTENT_VALIDATION_ENABLED=true: GET /api/platform/security/users with revoked Token A returns HTTP 401; IF false: Token A remains valid until its documented TTL elapses - assert that TTL behaviour, NOT a 401
[BODY] the 401 response (when asserted) does not leak user data or internal paths
[STATUS] GET /api/platform/security/users with active Token B returns HTTP 200 (revocation is scoped to Token A only)
Cross_Layer_Checks:
[API] Token A rejected after revocation; Token B unaffected
[NETWORK] No 5xx errors on any request
Failure_Signals: POST /revoke/token returns non-200; PERSISTENT_VALIDATION_ENABLED=true but revoked Token A still authorizes (real defect); PERSISTENT_VALIDATION_ENABLED=false but Token A is rejected before its TTL elapses (real defect); Token B also rejected after Token A revocation (over-broad invalidation); 500 errors
Cleanup: Obtain new token and use to clean up any test state
References: VCST-4576; Corrected 2026-09-19 (REG-2026-09-19-1035): /connect/revocation does not exist - its 404 is a non-endpoint, not a defect - replaced with /revoke/token. The 401 check also moved off /currentuser, which is [Authorize]+[AllowAnonymous] and can never 401. The precondition required EnablePersistentStorageTokenValidation=true but never verified it; it is now read live and the assertion branches on it (platform default is false - see BUG_032_057, config-gated by design).

Title: Persistent Access Token — Never-Issued Token Returns 401
Preconditions:
[PRE:CLEAR_SESSION]
- Platform accessible
- Authorization__EnablePersistentStorageTokenValidation=true configured
Steps:
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/users with Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJmYWtlIn0.invalidsignature
[WAIT] Receive response (expect 401)
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/users with Authorization: Bearer AAAA.BBBB.CCCC
[WAIT] Receive response (expect 401)
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/currentuser with no Authorization header
[WAIT] Receive response (expect 200, anonymous-allowed by design)
Assertions:
[STATUS] Both /api/platform/security/users requests (fabricated and malformed tokens) return HTTP 401
[BODY] No user data in either 401 response
[BODY] No internal paths or stack traces in either error response
[STATUS] /api/platform/security/currentuser with no Authorization header returns HTTP 200 BY DESIGN ([Authorize]+[AllowAnonymous], vc-platform SecurityController.cs:259-263) - an anonymous-contract check, never a 401 expectation
[BODY] the anonymous 200 response body is empty and leaks no user data
Cross_Layer_Checks:
[API] No 500 returned for malformed tokens against /api/platform/security/users
[NETWORK] Both /users requests fail with 401, not 200
Failure_Signals: 200 returned by /api/platform/security/users for a fabricated/unsigned token; 500 Internal Server Error instead of 401; user data visible in error response body; the currentuser anonymous 200 response leaks user data (breaks the anonymous contract)
Cleanup: none
References: VCST-4576; Corrected 2026-09-19 (REG-2026-09-19-1035): the 401 assertions targeted /api/platform/security/currentuser, which is [Authorize]+[AllowAnonymous] in vc-platform source and therefore can NEVER return 401 for any input - an unfalsifiable oracle. Re-pointed at the permission-gated /users endpoint; the anonymous contract is now asserted separately.

Title: Session Invalidation After Password Change — Other Devices Logged Out
Preconditions:
[PRE:CLEAR_SESSION]
- Authorization__EnablePersistentStorageTokenValidation=true configured (enables OpenIddict DB-based revocation)
- User account available (use agent pool slot 1 for Device A context, slot 2 for Device B context)
- Two separate sessions can be established for the same user
Steps:
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/connect/token for @td(ACME_BUYER.email) — obtain Token-A (Device A session)
[WAIT] Receive Token-A
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/connect/token for @td(ACME_BUYER.email) again — obtain Token-B (Device B session)
[WAIT] Receive Token-B
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/currentuser with Token-A (Device B still active — verify pre-change)
[ASSERT] Both tokens return 200 before password change
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/users/changepassword (or changePassword mutation via xAPI) using Token-A with currentPassword=@td(ACME_BUYER.password) and new password
[WAIT] Password change returns HTTP 200
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/currentuser with Token-B (Device B token — expect 401 after change)
[WAIT] Receive response
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/currentuser with Token-A (Device A token — should survive)
[WAIT] Receive response
Assertions:
[STATUS] Password change returns HTTP 200
[STATUS] Token-B returns HTTP 401 after password change (other-device session invalidated)
[BODY] Token-B 401 response contains no user data
[STATUS] Token-A continues to return HTTP 200 OR returns 401 (either is acceptable — behavior depends on platform implementation; the initiating-session-survives behavior is documented in VCST-4531 comment)
Cross_Layer_Checks:
[API] Token-B revoked after password change
[NETWORK] No 5xx errors
[ADMIN] Security > Users panel for the account shows no active authorizations for Token-B
Failure_Signals: Token-B still returns 200 after password change (invalidation not working); 500 errors on password change endpoint; Password change endpoint returns 4xx
Cleanup: Restore original password via admin API; clean up AGENT-TEST- sessions
References: VCST-4531
